title: The Last Delivery
summary: Kestrel wants word from the square, then one last bag of letters run out to the Wayfarer camp up the north road.
ask: Kestrel: There you are. You owe me word from the square. You're late, Runner.
Kestrel: The Association said you died. I said you'd be late to your own funeral.
Kestrel: So? What did you see?

done: Kestrel: A gate. Under the bells. Right.
Kestrel: Well. You brought it. Late, but you brought it.
Kestrel: One last bag. The camp up the north road has waited a week for its letters.
Kestrel: Out the High Gate. Hale will wave you through. Don't stop for sheep.
Hale: Licence? Fine. The Commons bite less than they look. Mostly.

steps.text: Run the letters to the Wayfarer camp up the north road

done: Ilse: Letters! With Kestrel's knot on them. She still ties them like she's angry at the string.
Ilse: Sit a minute. Nobody out here runs anywhere.
Ilse: First night out? Take a coal from our fire. Carry it till you find your ground, then set it down. It'll know.

steps.text: Set your Ember where you'd live
Back to Kestrel on the Roost
done: Kestrel: Good. That was your last bag. You don't run letters anymore.
Kestrel: You run at the things everyone else runs from. Come home when you can. The roof's still yours.
